intro: Two powerful forces reshaped martial arts in the twentieth century: the movie camera and the television contract. Films from Shanghai, Tokyo, Hong Kong and Hollywood gave audiences heroes, schools and styles. Some of those schools were real, with founders and records. Others were written for a script and then painted on the doors of real gyms.

Mixed martial arts grew from a different kind of screen. In 1993 a television company staged an eight-man tournament in Denver and sold it on pay-per-view. Within a few years, politicians called for bans. The sport survived by accepting rule books and licenses from state athletic commissions, the same offices that had overseen boxing since 1920.

In this unit you will read films as historical sources. You will learn to separate a studio's advertising from the record, and a legend from a dated document. You will also trace how a new league borrowed rooms from wrestling, boxing, judo and Muay Thai, and how laws in states like New Jersey, New York and Illinois shaped it.
bigQuestion: Who gets to name a style or run a sport: the people who film it, the people who sell it, or the people who regulate it?

timeline.t: Pankration joins the ancient Olympic Games, by tradition
New York's Walker Law creates a State Athletic Commission for boxing
Mingxing releases The Burning of the Red Lotus Temple in Shanghai
Kurosawa Akira's first film, Sanshiro Sugata, dramatizes the early Kodokan
Masahiko Kimura defeats Hélio Gracie at the Maracanã in Rio de Janeiro
Muhammad Ali and Antonio Inoki fight to a draw at the Nippon Budokan
The Karate Kid introduces the fictional dojo names Miyagi-do and Cobra Kai
UFC 1 is held in Denver and sold on pay-per-view
New York bans professional mixed martial arts
New Jersey and Nevada sanction MMA under written rules; Zuffa buys UFC
Ronda Rousey and Liz Carmouche fight the first women's UFC bout
New York repeals its ban, and UFC 205 is held at Madison Square Garden

test.q: Which Shanghai film of 1928 began a wave of sword-hero serials?
choices: The Burning of the Red Lotus Temple
test.why: The Mingxing company's 1928 film led to many sequels before censors banned such films.

test.q: Why do Hong Kong screen fights often look like acrobatics?
choices: Many fight performers trained in Peking opera
test.why: Performers from opera schools like the China Drama Academy carried stage methods into film.

test.q: Which director's first film was Sanshiro Sugata (1943)?
test.why: Kurosawa Akira directed Sanshiro Sugata for Toho in 1943.

test.q: What is the best evidence that a style existed before a film?
choices: Fan clubs formed after the film
A toy based on the film
Dated records of founders, places and students
test.why: Records older than the film, such as founders and dated photographs, show a real history.

test.q: Which name was created for the screenplay of The Karate Kid?
test.why: Miyagi-do and Cobra Kai are fictional dojo names from the film.

test.q: Which statement about the ninja image in films is best supported?
choices: Many historians link the black costume to kabuki stagehands
Ninjas were invented by Cannon Films
test.why: Few records describe a black costume; many historians connect it to kabuki kuroko.

test.q: What does the Shaolin stele of 728 show about The Shaolin Temple (1982)?
choices: Every scene in the film is documented
The film was made in the Tang dynasty
The film built a large story on a brief real record
test.why: The stele records the monks' help to Li Shimin; the film invented most of its story.

test.q: Where was UFC 1 held on November 12, 1993?
test.why: UFC 1 took place at McNichols Sports Arena in Denver.

test.q: Who taught judo to Carlos Gracie in Brazil?
test.why: Mitsuyo Maeda, a Kodokan judo expert, taught Carlos Gracie in Belém around 1917.

test.q: Which government office approves each professional MMA bout in a U.S. state?
test.why: State athletic commissions license fighters and sanction every professional bout.

test.q: Which board first wrote the Unified Rules of Mixed Martial Arts?
choices: The New York State Athletic Commission
The New Jersey State Athletic Control Board
test.why: New Jersey led the writing of the Unified Rules in 2000 and 2001.

test.q: Which law covers professional boxing but not MMA?
choices: The Muhammad Ali Boxing Reform Act of 2000
test.why: The Ali Act of 2000 sets national rules for boxing only.

test.q: Which state banned professional MMA in 1997 and lifted the ban in 2016?
test.why: New York's ban lasted from 1997 until a 2016 law signed by Governor Andrew Cuomo.

test.q: Which fighter was the first American woman to win an Olympic medal in judo?
test.why: Ronda Rousey won bronze in Beijing in 2008 and later fought the first women's UFC bout.

test.q: How is the UFC different from the International Judo Federation?
choices: Its members are national sports bodies
It is a private company answering to state law
test.why: The UFC is privately owned; the IJF is a federation of national bodies.

write.prompt: Is mixed martial arts a modern league or the return of an old tradition? Argue from at least three dated records in this unit, such as the UFC 1 event of 1993, the Unified Rules, New York's 1997 ban and 2016 repeal, or the Maeda–Gracie line.
tips: Name each record and its date, such as the Walker Law of 1920 or UFC 205 in 2016.
Label legends and marketing claims as claims, and set them beside documented facts.
Compare institutions: a federation, a private league and a state commission.
Use the unit's terms, such as sanction, corroboration and primary source.
